prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: システム連携用語表 (language ja).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "用語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 210px
  col 2: header "英語" · longest unbreakable word 103px · one-line width 163px
  col 3: header "説明" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 860px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A bilingual glossary for system-integration terms: readers identify a Japanese term, map it to its English equivalent, and read a short definition.","reading":"Scan down column 1 for the term, compare across to column 2 for the English label, then read column 3. Rows are the unit of comparison, so stable row starts and a readable term/translation pair matter more than equal column widths.","groups":["Columns 1–2 form the term/translation lookup pair and should stay adjacent with related widths.","Column 3 is a separate explanatory field and can absorb most wrapping."],"keep_intact":["English unbreakable tokens; column 2 needs at least 124px total for the 103px longest word.","Japanese terms as whole lookup keys where possible, ideally without splitting across more than 2–3 lines.","Headers 用語 / 英語 / 説明."],"may_wrap":["Column 3 descriptions at natural Japanese line breaks.","Multi-word English phrases at spaces, e.g. transaction manager / service level agreement.","Long Japanese terms at character boundaries only when necessary."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [92, 124, 143] · table 360×1151px · row heights [36, 153, 199, 153, 153, 153, 129, 176] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [84, 124, 151] · table 360×1151px · row heights [36, 153, 199, 153, 153, 153, 129, 176] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [76, 124, 159] · table 360×1035px · row heights [36, 153, 176, 129, 129, 129, 129, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
